debate.balLead: What we can't measure ourselves is an assumption. Here they are, with their source. Move them: the balance recomputes.
debate.chartSt: Pages served as static, per day
debate.daysLead: Two different scales: AI requests come in tens, pages served in thousands. Each bar is one day.
debate.early: Measurement started on {date}: the numbers are still too young to conclude. We publish them anyway, as they are.
debate.estNote: * estimate: measurement × assumption, adjustable in the balance.
debate.formula: AI = AI requests × Wh per request per page = (t_CMS − t_static) × P_core ÷ 3600 static = pages served × per page break-even = Wh per request ÷ per page
debate.hCms: CPU time of an uncached WordPress page
debate.hCmsSrc: Order of magnitude of a PHP render with its SQL queries.
debate.hGSrc: About 50 g CO₂e/kWh for the French grid; much more elsewhere.
debate.hStatic: Time to serve a static page
debate.hStaticSrc: Measured on our server, not an assumption.
debate.hW: Power of a busy server core
debate.hWSrc: Order of magnitude for a common server.
debate.hWhSrc: Google (August 2025): 0.24 Wh for a median Gemini request. Our generations are longer: this is a floor.
debate.intro: We use AI to create, and static to publish. One consumes, the other saves. Here are our real numbers, updated continuously, and the assumptions to read them. You judge.
debate.m1: Every AI request: kind, tokens, duration, failure
debate.m2: Every request served to a published site: page or file, size, serving time
debate.m3: The state of the tool: projects, blocks, translations, sites
debate.m4: The energy of an AI request
debate.m5: The computing time of an uncached WordPress page
debate.m6: The power of a server core, the carbon intensity
debate.m8: No IP, no cookie, no user-agent kept
debate.m9: Bots are recognised on the fly and counted apart

home.app_intro: Build a page with AI or import an existing site. Edit it with the mouse or in code, translate it, publish it. One tool, from the first word to the live address.
home.cta_login: Already have an account? Sign in
home.debate_desc: What AI consumes, what static saves: our real measurements and the assumptions to read them. You judge.
home.feat1_desc: Each block type (header, pricing, FAQ…) has its own AI. Describe what you want, watch the page write itself, compare three versions and keep the best.
home.feat2_desc: Pick your colours, fonts and corner radius: every block follows them. Change them and the whole page updates without touching the text.
home.feat3_desc: AI translates the page, you review it. If you regenerate a block, translations stay: only changed text needs translating again.
home.feat4_desc: Upload the .zip of an existing site — your WordPress static export, for instance. Click an element to select it, double-click to change its text, or ask the AI to change it. Prefer code? There's a real editor, with a file list and a live preview.
home.feat5_desc: Download an HTML file, a .zip site, or React and Vue components. Or publish to Netlify, Cloudflare or your own server: every save goes live right away.
home.home_intro: A WordPress site means a server, a database, plugins to update and security holes to watch. NADAPROD publishes static pages: nothing to hack, nothing to maintain. You build with AI, you translate, you publish.
home.marquee: GOODBYE WORDPRESS. / BACK TO STATIC. / NOTHING TO HACK. / NOTHING TO MAINTAIN. /
home.nada: Nothing in production but your pages.
home.network_intro: We act through our choices, and we share the method and the tool. The code is free (DWTFYW license, MIT-compatible): use it, change it, host it yourself. Below, sites already published with NADAPROD.
home.newsletter_more: Or fill in the full form
home.newsletter_sub: The public instance opens in waves. Leave your email, or install NADAPROD on your own server tonight: the code is free.
home.proof1: specialised AIs, one per block type
home.sendError: Could not send — try again or write to contact@nadaprod.com
home.services_subtitle: A CMS rebuilds every page on every visit, with a database, plugins and their security holes. A static site is files ready to serve. It's the best defence, and the leanest way to publish.
home.svc_log_desc: A visit is one file read and sent. No page rebuilt, no database queried, no third-party scripts. CSS trimmed to what's used, fonts served by your own site: less computing, less data sent, a small server is enough.
home.svc_prod_desc: No database, no code running on the server, no forgotten plugin. There is simply nothing to attack — and no security update to chase.
home.svc_safe_d1: Plain HTML, readable in twenty years

studio.conflictBody: This project was changed in another tab or on another device. Reload the page to start from the latest version: your very last changes here will not be saved.
studio.errStreamCut: The generation was cut off before completion
studio.err_auth_body: The server cannot authenticate with Gemini. To fix server-side: GEMINI_API_KEY in the .env file, then restart.
studio.err_blocked_body: Gemini's safety filters blocked this request. Rephrase the brief.
studio.err_empty_body: The model returned nothing usable (filtered or truncated). Retrying often works; otherwise simplify the brief.
studio.err_invalid_body: Gemini rejected the request (unknown model or invalid parameters). Check server-side: GEMINI_MODEL.
studio.err_network_body: The link to the server or to Gemini was cut.
studio.err_quota_body: The generation service hit its limit (requests per minute or daily quota). Wait a moment; if it persists, check the Gemini key's quota and billing.
studio.err_rate_limited_body: Too many generations in a row from your account. This limit protects the shared quota.
studio.err_timeout_body: The model did not answer in time. Retry, possibly with a shorter brief.
studio.err_upstream_body: The generation service returned an error. This is usually temporary.
